title: Specialise the PDO Atiyah-Singer theorem to the elliptic differential operator
intent: Prove the Atiyah-Singer index equality for an elliptic differential operator by specialising the general PDO index theorem (PseudodifferentialOperator.index_eq_cotangentTopologicalIndex) to the operator's own toPseudodifferentialOperator, deriving the homogeneous representative and its ellipticity from the principal polynomial rather than assuming them.
also_known_as: instantiate a general theorem at a concrete instance

parent.name: index_eq_cotangentTopologicalIndex
parent.statement:
theorem index_eq_cotangentTopologicalIndex (hP : P.IsElliptic) :
    P.analyticIndex hP = cotangentTopologicalIndex n M (P.symbolKClass μ R hP)

children.name: principalSymbol_eq_regularizedSymbol
children.statement:
theorem principalSymbol_eq_regularizedSymbol
    (A : QuantizationPresentation (n := n) (r := r) (q := q) E F) :
    (P.toPseudodifferentialOperator μ).principalSymbol =
      globalPrincipalSymbolClass E F (m : ℝ)
        (A.regularizedSymbol (m : ℝ) P.principalSymbolFunction
          P.isSmoothOffZeroGlobalSymbol_principalSymbolFunction
          P.isHomogeneousGlobalSymbol_principalSymbolFunction)

children.name: isElliptic_iff_isEllipticGlobalSymbol
children.statement:
theorem isElliptic_iff_isEllipticGlobalSymbol :
    P.IsElliptic ↔ IsEllipticGlobalSymbol E F P.principalSymbolFunction

children.name: isElliptic_iff_homogeneous
children.statement:
theorem isElliptic_iff_homogeneous (R : QuantizationPresentation (n := n) (r := r) (q := q) E F)
    (a : homogeneousGlobalSymbolSpace (n := n) (r := r) (q := q) E F m)
    (hP : P.principalSymbol = globalPrincipalSymbolClass E F m
      (R.regularizedSymbol m a.val a.property.1 a.property.2)) :
    P.IsElliptic ↔ IsEllipticGlobalSymbol E F a.val
children.closed_by: exact (P.isElliptic_iff_of_principalSymbol_eq (R.regularizedSymbol m a.val a.property.1 a.property.2) hP).trans (isEllipticFullGlobalSymbol_regularizedSymbol_iff R m a.val a.property.1 a.property.2)

children.name: PseudodifferentialOperator.index_eq_cotangentTopologicalIndex
children.statement:
theorem PseudodifferentialOperator.index_eq_cotangentTopologicalIndex {m : ℝ}
    (P : PseudodifferentialOperator (n := n) (r := r) (q := q) E F μ m)
    (R : QuantizationPresentation (n := n) (r := r) (q := q) E F)
    (a : homogeneousGlobalSymbolSpace (n := n) (r := r) (q := q) E F m)
    (hp : P.principalSymbol = globalPrincipalSymbolClass E F m
      (R.regularizedSymbol m a.val a.property.1 a.property.2)) (hi : P.IsElliptic) :
    P.toLinearMap.index =
      cotangentTopologicalIndex n M (P.symbolKClassOfHomogeneous R a hp hi)
children.closed_by: have heval := PseudodifferentialOperator.analyticIndexOfComponents_symbolKClassOfHomogeneous μ P R a hp hi; rw [analyticIndexOfComponents_eq_cotangentTopologicalIndex μ] at heval; exact heval.symm

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem about a specific object (an elliptic differential operator P) whose conclusion, P.analyticIndex hP = cotangentTopologicalIndex n M (P.symbolKClass μ R hP), is exactly the instance of a general theorem P.toLinearMap.index = cotangentTopologicalIndex n M (P.symbolKClassOfHomogeneous R a hp hi) already proved for a more general class (PDOs carrying a supplied homogeneous representative a, principal-symbol equality hp and ellipticity hi).
applicability.use_when: a general theorem over the weaker/more general structure already exists; the specific object embeds into it by a definitional map (P.toPseudodifferentialOperator μ); and the instantiation data — the homogeneous representative and the two ellipticity certificates — can be derived from the specific object's own principal data by named boundary lemmas rather than assumed.
applicability.avoid_when: the specific-to-general embedding is not definitional, so the boundary facts need deep proofs of their own; the general theorem's hypotheses are not discharged by the specific structure (here the homogeneous representative and its ellipticity would then have to be added as assumptions); or the general theorem does not exist yet, in which case instantiation is re-proving rather than reuse.

The same three-step specialisation is performed again in the same file by the sibling definition symbolKClass: it assembles the homogeneous representative a, derives hp via principalSymbol_eq_regularizedSymbol and hi via the two ellipticity equivalences, then applies the PDO construction.

consequences: The move concentrates the proof burden in four boundary lemmas and leaves the main theorem a thin glue: the parent's proof body (lines 126-138) only assembles the homogeneous representative and passes it to the general PDO theorem. Obligations created: every hypothesis of the general theorem must be discharged for the specific operator — the PDO (P.toPseudodifferentialOperator μ, definitional), the homogeneous representative a (assembled inline from P.principalSymbolFunction and its certificates), the principal-symbol equality hp (principalSymbol_eq_regularizedSymbol) and PDO ellipticity hi (isElliptic_iff_homogeneous composed with isElliptic_iff_isEllipticGlobalSymbol). Failure mode: if the specific-to-general embedding were not definitional, or if the general theorem demanded data the specific object cannot supply (a Hermitian metric, positive order, or equal bundle ranks — all explicitly excluded in the docstring), the instantiation would fail and the boundary lemmas would need real proofs of their own.
